title: Dispatch CUS 4: Eviction Notices Arrive from Addresses in the Other City
summary: Both sets of residents are instructed to leave homes occupying the same ground.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Residents of North Loom Street received notices yesterday ordering them to vacate by 20 February. The forms bear the seal of Alderwick’s Office of Improvements, an office that does not exist in the city’s present administration. They say the properties will be cleared to restore Vesper Row.

Across the new doors, residents of Vesper Row have received equivalent notices bearing the seal of Alderwick’s current council. That council issued none. Miss Morrow examined both sets. Each seal is authentic to the government using it on its own side. Each notice is directed at people the issuing office does not recognize.

Beatrice Hume, the registrar for the other Alderwick, crossed into Miss Morrow’s office carrying her own census volume. It lists the twenty-three households on Fenwick Lane and Vesper Row as ordinary residents. Where our volume counts the courtyards and North Loom Street, hers has blank space filled by a pencilled word: “encroachment.”

Miss Hume says her council’s surveyors are worried about the same shifting walls. They did not order the notices. She believes a routine set of forms was prepared when her clerks marked conflicting addresses for review. “A system made to remove an error has decided that people are the error,” she said.

Alderman Felix Dorne has suspended enforcement of every notice carrying his council’s seal. Miss Hume promises to seek the same order at home. Inspector Daniel Voss has asked both registrars to warn him immediately if a wall or floor moves again.
